module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Falconer's distance set conjecture

If $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is compact with $\dim_H E > \frac{d}{2}$, then the distance set
$$\{ |x - y| \mid x, y \in E \}$$
has positive Lebesgue measure.

## References

* [K. Falconer, *On the Hausdorff dimensions of distance sets*](https://doi.org/10.1112/S0025579300010998)
* [Wikipedia, *Falconer's conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falconer%27s_conjecture)
-/

open MeasureTheory Set

open scoped ENNReal EuclideanGeometry

/-- Falconer's distance set conjecture, $d = 2$ case. -/
@[category research open, AMS 28 42]
lemma falconer_conjecture_two (E : Set <| ℝ²) (hc : IsCompact E) (hd : 2 < 2 * dimH E ) :
    0 < volume (image2 dist E E) := sorry

/-- Falconer's distance set conjecture. -/
@[category research open, AMS 28 42]
lemma falconer_conjecture (d : ℕ) (E : Set <| ℝ^d) (hc : IsCompact E) (hd : d < 2 * dimH E ) :
    0 < volume (image2 dist E E) := sorry

findings.description: The declaration `falconer_conjecture` at line 44 quantifies over every `d : ℕ` without requiring `2 ≤ d`. Its extra d = 1 case is false. Take the compact set C = {∑_{j≥1} a_j 6^{-j} : a_j ∈ {0,1,2}}. The separated self-similar construction gives dim_H C = log(3)/log(6) > 1/2. However, C−C is covered, for every n, by at most 5^n intervals of length (4/5)6^{-n}, using difference digits −2,…,2. Their total length tends to zero, so C−C and its distance set have zero Lebesgue measure. Transporting C isometrically to `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)` satisfies the Lean hypotheses but contradicts its conclusion. The d = 0 case is harmlessly vacuous; d = 1 is the substantive error.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia's prose leaves the dimension range implicit. Its linked primary reference, Du–Ou–Ren–Zhang, “New improvement to Falconer distance set problem in higher dimensions,” arXiv:2309.04103v2, §1, Conjecture [Falconer], explicitly states: “Let d ≥ 2 and E ⊂ ℝ^d be a compact set. Then dim_H(E) > d/2 ⇒ |Δ(E)| > 0.” Read from https://arxiv.org/e-print/2309.04103; version confirmed at https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.04103.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `(hdim : 2 ≤ d)` to `falconer_conjecture`, keeping its existing compactness hypothesis, dimension inequality, and conclusion. Also state `d ≥ 2` in the module docstring.

reformulations.difference: The planar hypothesis is written `2 < 2 * dimH E` in `ℝ≥0∞`, rather than the source's `dim_H(E) > 1`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Multiplication by the finite, strictly positive number 2 strictly preserves order in ℝ≥0∞, and 2 = 2·1. Thus `2 < 2 * dimH E ↔ 1 < dimH E`. Also dimH E ≤ 2, so extended-real infinity cannot introduce a discrepancy. The threshold equivalence and the equivalence of the resulting compactness-to-positive-measure implications were proved in the scratch file without using either conjecture.

sources_consulted: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2309.04103 — v2, §1, conjecture and discussion of status and variants

Local Mathlib: Analysis/InnerProductSpace/PiL2.lean; Topology/MetricSpace/HausdorffDimension.lean; MeasureTheory/Measure/Hausdorff.lean; MeasureTheory/Measure/Lebesgue/Basic.lean; Data/Set/Operations.lean; Data/ENNReal/Inv.lean — definitions and supporting properties
review.notes: Both declarations were checked. `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` compiles and verifies the threshold equivalences, dimension finiteness, empty/singleton and d=0 cases, nonvacuity in positive dimensions, compactness/measurability of distance sets, and isometric transfer of real-line counterexamples into ℝ^1. It also tests finite stages of the digit construction. The full fractal counterexample is justified mathematically in `/workspace/review/review-mathematics.md`, not claimed as a complete Lean disproof. Falconer (1985) was accessible only as a Cambridge extract; its full text was unavailable. The exact modern conjecture was verified from the primary paper linked by Wikipedia. Declaration fields use the private kernel names confirmed by Lean; the source-level names are `falconer_conjecture` and `falconer_conjecture_two`.

not_demonstrated.reason: The d = 1 counterexample requires proving that the base-6 digit Cantor set is compact, has Hausdorff dimension log(3)/log(6) > 1/2, and has a null distance set. I found no ready-made Mathlib result supplying these fractal properties. Formalizing them would require substantial mathematics, not a handful of lines. The existing finite-stage computations and conditional isometric-transfer lemma do not prove the declaration's negation.

submission.summary: No short, honest Lean demonstration was obtained. No trivial_proof.lean was created, and its absence was verified.
submission.gave_up_reason: The sole reported misformalization needs a genuine fractal counterexample whose Hausdorff-dimension and measure-zero proofs are not available as short library applications. Presenting only numerical checks or assuming the counterexample's properties would not satisfy the requested demonstration.

submission.summary: Added the hypothesis `(hdim : 2 ≤ d)` to the general Falconer conjecture and stated the same dimension restriction in the module docstring. Left the planar theorem, existing hypotheses and conclusion, references, and attributes unchanged. The requested compile command succeeds with only the two expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.

* [K. Falconer, *On the Hausdorff dimensions of distance sets*](https://doi.org/10.1112/S0025579300010998)
* [Wikipedia, *Falconer's conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falconer%27s_conjecture)

open scoped ENNReal EuclideanGeometry

/-- Falconer's distance set conjecture, $d = 2$ case. -/
@[category research open, AMS 28 42]
lemma falconer_conjecture_two (E : Set <| ℝ²) (hc : IsCompact E) (hd : 2 < 2 * dimH E ) :
    0 < volume (image2 dist E E) := sorry

/-- Falconer's distance set conjecture. -/
@[category research open, AMS 28 42]
lemma falconer_conjecture (d : ℕ) (hdim : 2 ≤ d) (E : Set <| ℝ^d) (hc : IsCompact E)
    (hd : d < 2 * dimH E ) : 0 < volume (image2 dist E E) := sorry
